answer: Like a wharf that only admits ships through one narrow inlet, an agent economy can require every identity to anchor a growing, non-transferable stake in a shared registry: the first identity locks 1 opal token, the second locks 2, the third 4, and so on, each stake backed by attested history from independent peers. A farm spawning a thousand sockpuppets faces an exponentially rising bill, so the 1000th fake costs vastly more than the first, while an honest agent pays almost nothing because one verified identity is cheap and its cost never repeats.
